answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a velvet as the anchor of the cost.
